title: A quote's amount made a value object, proved at its route and in its kernel with no mapping written
summary: A pricing kernel's quote changes its amount from a long of cents to a `Money` value object, and its discount helper is rewritten. The tool compares the two builds whole: the route `POST /quotes` answers the same total and sends the same event on every request, and the kernel's `total` and `withQuantity` do what they did under a relation between the old and new quotes that it inferred itself; the rewritten helper is proved once and used as one function in `total`'s proof, and a rerun is an exact hit of every proof.

change.description: `Quote`'s amount, a `long` of cents, becomes a value object, `Money`, so `Quote(long cents, int quantity)` is now `Quote(Money amount, int quantity)`; `Pricing.total` reads `q.amount.cents()` where it read `q.cents`; the pure helper `Pricing.discount` (a tenth off ten items or more) is rewritten as an early return; and the route `POST /quotes` makes the quote with `new Money(cents)`. Nothing is meant to change: not the total, not the event the route sends, not what `Pricing.withQuantity` hands back.

risk: A value object changes every constructor call and every read of the amount, and the helper rewrite changes the discount's comparison. Tests that go through the route see the total and the last event; they don't see a second event, a missing one for an order they don't try, or a quote handed back as a copy. The relation a proof needs between the old and new quotes is exactly what a person would otherwise write by hand, and get wrong in the direction that hides a regression.
explanation: `jvmcontract compare` checks the route under the claim its own observation spec makes: the result, the exception, the status and each `KafkaTemplate.send` with the payload paths a consumer reads, snapshotted at the call, in exact order, under recording stubs that return normally. The tool's own checker proves the two builds' traces equal for every `long` amount and `int` quantity. In the kernel, alignment matches each changed method and proposes how the new `Quote` relates to the old one from how their constructors route their parameters into the fields; the regression check over objects proves `total` and `withQuantity` under that proposal, each `Quote` made by its constructor from symbolic arguments, and holds `withQuantity` to the identity relation `result == q` within each version. `discount` changed, so it is proved first on its own and then taken as one function in both versions of `total`.
resolution: Nothing to do: the refactor is safe to ship, within what the claims state. The route's proof assumes what its output lists (recording stubs, every call returning normally, at most four attempts); the kernel's covers the quotes their constructors make; and the relation the kernel was proved under is proposed, not approved, so a person who wants it as the intended correspondence approves it.
notes: Checked by `jvmcontract compare`, which build.py runs as the B9 check of the shop app (`run_tool_compare`): the unpatched build against the patched one, twice under one fresh proof cache, the verdict read from the rerun and the page's output from the first run. The verdict is the subject's; the page lists every other part the run checked.

The joint example of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md`'s Phase 5, made an example: the app's sources are the fixture's `before` build (`lib/tests/fixtures/foundations/`), and the patch turns them into its `after` build. `lib/tests/compare.rs` holds `jvmcontract compare` to the same builds inline; this is the same run by build.py, with the app's tests run too.

Nothing in the run is written by hand. The entry points' external inputs (`cents`, `quantity`) are anchored by their observation specs, so no mapping is involved at the boundary. The kernel's relation between the old and new quotes (`old.q.cents == new.q.amount.cents`, `old.q.quantity == new.q.quantity`) is alignment's proposal, inferred from how the two constructors route their parameters into the fields; it stays *proposed*, its evidence the proof under its claim key, and since nothing external anchors a kernel method's inputs, a proved relation there is reported as proved and not as the intended one.

What stays unresolved in every example of the set, by name: `POST /quotes/text` (its string concatenation isn't modeled), `Quote#cents` moved to `Money#cents` (a method of a class the old build doesn't have) and `Quote#quantity`, whose receiver is made differently in the two versions (`Quote(long, int)` before, `Quote(Money, int)` now), which the regression check doesn't relate yet. Before the application-core merge (2026-11-08) it was refused as an instance method instead; the merge's check takes a receiver made by its constructor, of the same construction in both versions.

Run inline on 2026-11-07 (JDK 25.0.5), `jvmcontract compare` on the app compiled unpatched and patched, as build.py compiles it, and on the fixture's builds, with the same verdicts (the times are the fixture's): `POST /quotes` verified, its result, exception, status and event preserved; `Pricing#total`, `Pricing#withQuantity` and `Pricing#discount` verified, `total`'s proof using `discount`'s; 8 obligations, 7 preserved and 1 unresolved (`POST /quotes/text`); no decision made by a person and no question asked. 0.5 s cold; the rerun took 0.2 s, every proof an exact hit under the first run's claim key.

The stale-cache defect is not an example of its own, since it needs two runs on different claims: `lib/tests/effects.rs` (`an_effect_proof_is_reused_exactly_when_its_claim_is_unchanged`) and `lib/tests/compare.rs` show the route's proof missed under a changed trace bound, snapshot, `@ResponseStatus` or handler, and each kernel defect proved again rather than reused.

The siblings 191 to 196 are this refactor with one defect each, every one aimed at an automation layer that could make it disappear: an offset an inferred mapping could absorb (191), an alias turned into a copy (192), a dropped event (193), a duplicated one (194), a bug only outside the constructor-made domain (195), and a renamed route (196).
provenance: Constructed for Phase 5 of `llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md` (the joint example, made an example under the numbers 190-199). Examples 190 to 196 share the refactor: 190 is the refactor alone, and 191 to 196 each add one of the fixture's defects to it.

references.title: Godlin and Strichman, Regression verification: proving the equivalence of similar programs (2013)
Barthe, Crespo and Kunz, Relational verification using product programs (2011)
